blogs.title: Multiphasic Anaphylaxis Unveiled: Why Some Reactions Keep Coming Back
blogs.description: Explore why a subset of anaphylaxis patients experience multiple recurrences even after apparent resolution—reviewing definitions across major guideline bodies, reported incidence ranges (0.4‑23 %), timing windows (first 24 h up to almost 80 h), and key clinical clues that separate true biphasics from ongoing residual exposure.

blogs.title: "Half‑Dose Dilemma": Why Adult Auto‑Injectors Might Under‑Treat Your Patient
blogs.description: Contrast guideline‐recommended weight‐based epinephrine dosing (0.01 mg/kg up to 0.5 mg) with common adult auto‑injector contents (0·3 mg). Discuss real‐world consequences demonstrated by recent retrospective data showing higher rates of escalation when patients initially receive the lower dose—and practical ways to choose or stock appropriate devices.

blogs.title: "Corticosteroids Reconsidered": The Emerging Evidence Against Routine Use in Anaphylaxis
blogs.description: Summarise systematic reviews demonstrating lack of benefit—or even harm—in preventing biphenatic reactions when corticosteroids are given prophylactically after an allergic event, clarify why contemporary guidelines now advise against their routine use while highlighting select situations where short courses might still be justified.

blogs.title: "Mast Cell Disorders Hidden in Plain Sight" — Recognising Systemic Mastocytosis Among Overlooked Patients
blogs.description: Explain how elevated baseline and peak tryptase levels can signal systemic mastocytosis—a disease predisposing patients to severe or multiphasic reactions—outlining major/minor diagnostic criteria, interpreting key lab thresholds, and outlining the workup roadmap once suspicion rises.

blogs.title: "Tryptase Timings Matter" — Best Practices for Sampling Triggers Without Delaying Urgent Treatment
blogs.description: Detail the ideal sampling schedule required by current guidelines (pre-treatment ASAP if feasible; second sample within 1–2 h during peak symptoms; third ≥24 h after resolution), discuss practical ways to obtain specimens without compromising care, and illustrate how delayed sampling can blur diagnosis.

blogs.title: "Turning the Tide" — Continuous IV Epinephrine Infusion Versus Repeat IM Doses During Multiphasic Episodes
blogs.description: Present a structured decision framework weighing risks/benefits when one faces recurrent anaphylactic crises despite adequate initial therapy—examining continuous bedside infusions versus repeated balanced-IP injections—including evidence gaps, monitoring requirements, and real‑world scenarios derived from contemporary case reports.
